checks.name: real fixture: commerce integration suite against t69
checks.result: OK (13 tests, 145 assertions). The PR body recorded 12 tests / 140 assertions before this round; the new test is test_audit_rows_are_swept_once_past_their_retention: the daily event is on the schedule, firing the real cron hook deletes an audit row backdated past 90 days and leaves a one-day-old row in place. The other 12 prove the push chain unchanged (batch apply + audit row, unknown SKU per-row error, idempotent re-push with zero stock actions, out-of-stock gate + recovery through the real cart, state_overridden/not_stock_managed, the three key states).

checks.name: retention: unit trio and sweep (WP_Mock)
checks.result: OK (6 tests, 155 assertions). The daily event is scheduled when missing; an event already on the schedule is left alone (no second daily event); deactivation clears it; the sweep deletes the expired rows oldest-first and keeps the fresh one, with the query asserted (private linker_stock_batch, IDs, page 1, date ASC, post_date_gmt before the 90-day cutoff, wp_delete_post with force); a full batch is followed by another and the walk stops at the short one; an empty window is asked once.

checks.name: instance: the sweep on the real WP-Cron path
checks.command: just wp t69 cron event list --fields=hook,next_run_relative,recurrence; just wp t69 cron event run linker_commerce_stock_batch_sweep; row count of linker_stock_batch before/after
checks.result: linker_commerce_stock_batch_sweep listed with recurrence '1 day'; the event ran ('Executed the cron event … in 0.065s'), row count 69 before and 69 after — every row on the instance is younger than the retention, so the sweep deleted nothing and left the audit trail intact. (Also listed: tv_b2b_stock_mirror_nightly, the inactive old plugin's event, which fires into the void and disappears with the old system at cutover — same observation as the #67 archive.)
